title: Increased sensitivity of Euplotes crassus to selective agents using glucose culture conditions
author: Lawrence A. Klobutcher
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2ahgab6

steps.title: Pellet Dunaliella algae
steps.instruction: Distribute a dense culture of Dunaliella salina into two 50 ml screw‑cap centrifuge tubes, then centrifuge at 1,000 RPM (~200 × g) for 2 min in a clinical centrifuge to pellet the algae.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and resuspend
steps.instruction: Discard all but the final 2.5 ml of supernatant from each tube, resuspend each algae pellet, and combine the two suspensions.

steps.title: Add Euplotes and glucose
steps.instruction: To the combined algae suspension add 2.5 ml log‑phase Euplotes crassus culture (grown with Dunaliella in artificial seawater) and 45 ml freshly prepared 0.3 M glucose (using deionized water).

steps.title: Add selective agent
steps.instruction: Introduce the desired selective agent to reach the final concentration of either 200 µg/µl G418, 200 µg/ml paromomycin, or 40 µg/ml puromycin.

steps.title: Distribute into plates
steps.instruction: Aliquot the cell mixture into microtiter plates, e.g., 2 ml per well of a 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Incubate humidified
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature in a humidified chamber (e.g., plastic box with wet paper towels or a beaker of water); cell death is observed within 2–3 days.
